newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Troops of Operation Sathjaya III repulsed massive counter attack by Tamil Tiger rebels on Thursday morning, say defense officials. The military on Wednesday advanced one kilometre from Murusumuddai, an important road junction in the northern Kilinochchi district, they said.
Troops smash massive Tiger counter thrust on Thursday morning, and "Their human wave tactics didn't work," a major general told The Island.
Troops of Operation Sthjaya III capture strategic junction on Kilinochchi-Paranthan road, on Wednesday.
Ten internationally known paedophiles have come to Sri Lanka, senior police officials say.
Troops of Operation Sathjaya III caputure important junction on Kilinochchi-Paranthan highway, defence officials say.
Archbishop of Colombo Kenneth Fernando urges Tamil rebels to give up arms and come forth for talks with government.

Government will not talk with Tamil rebels as their primary objective remains a separate homeland, Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar tells press conference in New York. Kadirgamar is in the United States to address the United Nations.
Tamil civilians in the suburbs of Kilinochchi flee as army and rebels remain locked in battle for fifth day in a row.
